The boot wait is deadline-bounded, with no per-seat multiplication of the60s wait in the serial follower. The late guard adds one registry/lease read only for a would-be lapse restart. No new periodic tick, poll, process launch or task fan-out appears. No demonstrated normal-use resource-cost breach blocks this head. This performance verdict does not clear the independent correctness/security ordering questions.

Verified cost:
- unheard_since_boot adds one relaxed atomic read and deadline arithmetic on each on_lapse invocation. During the boot window only, it also locks the existing lease map and checks one seat ID; after the deadline it returns before taking that lock. It performs no registry/store read or process probe.
- The requested sleep is until native_started_at + one configured extension lease (60s by default), not now +60s for every seat. The normal follower awaits each decision serially, so at most one of its boot sleeps is active; after the first reaches that shared deadline, later unheard seats add no further lease-length sleep. The sleep holds neither the global native lock nor the per-seat auth slot. A heartbeat arriving during it does not wake it early; the receiver is rechecked after the deadline.
- This is one conditional ONE-SHOT Tokio sleep/timer, not a new periodic timer or poll. Its configured deadline is bounded; total recovery latency is not guaranteed <=60s. Scheduler lateness, queued serial decisions, store/process/composer reads, recording and control admission remain outside that sleep bound. The existing scan roster/subscription can remain live while the serial follower sleeps; no new task-per-seat queue is created.
- The early F268 guard uses native_receiver_renewed. The late F274 guard uses it again ONLY for Cause::ExtensionLost when the candidate action is Restart. Thus at most TWO guard calls, not two on every path. Each takes the global native mutex, does registry.get (schema PRAGMA + keyed SELECT/decode), then locks the lease map for an identity/elapsed check. A would-be restart has four store statements across these guard calls, plus on_lapse's separate original registry.get and other existing decision work. F274's incremental late cost is one of those calls; the shared native critical section includes its store await.
- The auth slot is held during the late check, but the native lock is dropped before record/accept_control. No new lock spans control admission. A renewal found by the late check removes subsequent restart write/queue work; reports do not take that guard.
- The inherited cost-row corrections are accepted: every renewing heartbeat checks the owed set, even empty; pruning runs on the existing receiver-reconcile5s/deadline cadence using its existing roster, with up to owed x live-Copilot-roster comparisons. The20s heartbeat cadence is a default client recommendation, not a server request-rate limit. The10s completion-based brake still caps only gap reconciles, not all live lapse/heartbeat work.
- No F274 work is added to every receiver tick or per live seat per tick. A lapsed event/boot-gap decision supplies the trigger. Existing process-liveness fallback and restart/control launches are not new sites.

Nonblocking notes owed:
1. Say "no new periodic timer", not literally "no timer": sleep_until registers the bounded one-shot boot wait. State the shared default60s deadline separately from end-to-end serial-follower/restart latency. The source bound is not a live latency guarantee.
2. Price "up to two lease guards", each with a registry read: the late guard is restart-only, and the independent initial registry read remains. Keep read calls distinct from SQL statements and the native-lock hold time.
3. Preserve an authorized AFTER with bootstrap/gap decision counts, wait durations and complete guard/store work. This review deliberately triggered no working-seat lapse, heartbeat or boot.

Shutdown: the existing shutdown path aborts the lapse follower and then awaits it; the boot sleep is ordinary cancellable async waiting, so that path need not wait for its60s deadline. This is source-path verification, not a live full-shutdown/F267 timing witness.

Policy/brakes: lapse remains the policy input. The shared boot wait delays, and the late lease/error guard only spares; removing either permits more/earlier restart work. They are BRAKES, not a new retention policy.
